input.summary:
P4 hall (parts/room-31.mjs): 1-wide corridor x72 z14..20 furnished with a coat stand (spruce fence post and standing lantern) at the far end z20, the focal piece in the doorway's line of sight, plus hanging lanterns at z15 and z19. The lane z14..19 at y2..3 stays clear, and the z18 doorway cell is left empty.
make.sh runs whole and the part places 4 blocks with no refusals and no off-palette blocks. Room check reports NEEDS WORK only because the shell parts are absent in this copy.
Carpets and banners are not in palette.json, so the coat rack has no banner and no rugs.
left: Room check cannot pass in this copy: the shell parts (shell west/east, stairs, fittings) are stubs here, so the hall has no floor block at y1, no ceiling at y5 and no front door at (72,2..3,13). Both hanging lanterns (72,4,15) and (72,4,19) read as floating until the upper floor at y5 is built above them. Re-run `$MCD room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P4 hall"` after the shell merges.

Walk and FIT must be re-checked after merge: the hall is open to the living room (x71) and parlour (x73) at z14..17 and to the dining room and kitchen at z19..20. Their furniture must not block x72 z14..19 at y2..3, which is the lane to the rear doorway at z18.
No banner on the coat stand and no carpet runner: neither is in palette.json, so the coat rack reads as a lamp post on a fence rather than a coat rack.

waste.what: Checking the hall's floor, ceiling and door cells one by one with an inline node script to find out whether the shell existed in this copy.
waste.cost: one extra node call, about 8 cell lookups
waste.tool: `mcd room` should print a SHELL line (floor and ceiling cells the room box needs but are missing, and whether the door cell is built) so a designer knows at once that a verdict is blind.

waste.what: Working out the single-column layout by hand (rows along z, one character per cell at x72) before writing the layers() call.
waste.cost: one design pass, 7 rows x 3 layers
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could accept a `--layers` mode that prints the 3-D free grid of a one-cell-wide corridor, so the furnisher draws y levels directly.

companions.task: Check the hall's hanging lanterns against the finished upper floor at y5 and balance light across the corridor and the neighbouring living and parlour rooms, so no cell at the z14..20 lane goes dark once the openings are in.

companions.role: interior furnisher for the P4 living room and parlour
companions.task: Keep the x71 and x73 openings at z14..17 and the x72 lane at y2..3 free of furniture, so the hall stays walkable from the front door to the rear doorway at z18.
